text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- State comptroller to report soon on conduct of Labour party chief Ehud Barak when he was army chief during the training accident in 1992 in which five soldiers were killed and six wounded.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to clear air with Foreign Minister David Levy.
- Former Finance Minister Dan Meridor: I may challenge Netanyahu to Likud leadership.
- Rabin assassination dashed peace with Syria -- U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk.
- World Bank tries to combat unemployment problem in Gaza, West Bank.
- Police: Israel is a global money-laundering centre.
- Communications Minister Limor Livnat, Bezeq clash over price-cut notice.
- New England Patriots' owner invests $40 million in Caesarea plant.
- Officials: Labour unrest might hurt defence industries' income.
- Tnuva food cooperative discussing purchase of foreign know-how.
- El Al adopts new plan for aircraft replacement.
GLOBES
- Demand for foreign currency continues: Dollar representative rate rises by 0.51 percent to 3.524 shekels.
- Labour and Social Affairs Minister Eli Yishai: 1997 jobless rate might hit 8.5 percent.
HAARETZ

- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai warns: "The Palestinian Authority interested in inflammability in the terroitories". Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat invites heads of security establishment to an emergency night-time meeting.
- Prime minister plans to change calculation for housing in monthly consumer price index, claiming present method causes artificial rise in pace of inflation.
- Fear of air accidents at Tel Aviv's Ben-Gurion Airport due to shortage of flight paths.
MAARIV
- Banks supervisor Zeev Abeles says there's no chance undesirable elements will control banks in Israel.
- Divorced wife of Benjamin Netanyahu's late brother Yoni writes letter critical of prime minister.
- Sarah Netanyahu in outburst during stormy interview with Israel TV: "Other politicians cheated on their wives also."
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman tells cabinet ministers: Stop fighting and save the peace.
- Dollar at 3.54 shekels -- a rise of 8.7 percent since the start of the year.
- Sources close to Foreign Minister David Levy quoted as saying bringing Ariel Sharon into inner cabinet is like putting a bull in a china shop.
